$comment: Published expansion vector for bye.fun's roll draw. h = sha256(randomness || k || a); x = the low 16 bytes of h read little-endian; bound = the largest multiple of w below 2^128; accept r = x mod w when x < bound, else retry with a+1; after 4 attempts reduce the last word regardless. `attempts` is a 1-based count, so the attempt byte on the deciding hash is `attempts - 1`. `w`, `r` are decimal strings because they exceed the range JSON numbers carry exactly. This file is the artifact an independent verifier is checked against; it is generated from the written formula, never from the program.

cases.name: live-pool-first-attempt
cases.note: A realistic pool weight: 40 leaves at the admission floor plus 3/2/1 blanks. The rejection region here is about 2^-78 of the range, so acceptance is immediate.

cases.name: live-pool-later-roll
cases.note: The same batch randomness and the same pool at roll 7 — the roll index is what separates the draws of one batch.

cases.name: rejection-accepts-on-attempt-2
cases.note: A weight one past half the range: 2^128 mod w is w-2, so nearly half of all words are rejected and the sampler reaches a later attempt deterministically.

cases.name: rejection-accepts-on-attempt-3
cases.note: A weight one past half the range: 2^128 mod w is w-2, so nearly half of all words are rejected and the sampler reaches a later attempt deterministically.

cases.name: rejection-exhausts-the-cap
cases.note: Every one of the four attempts is rejected, so the last word is reduced regardless and the full cap is recorded.

cases.name: weight-one
cases.note: A single unit of weight: 2^128 mod 1 is 0, there is no rejection region, and the only possible draw is 0.

cases.name: weight-divides-the-range
cases.note: 2^127 divides 2^128 exactly, so the acceptance bound is the whole range and no word can ever be rejected.

cases.name: weight-is-the-whole-range-less-one
cases.note: The largest weight a u128 can express. 2^128 mod w is 1, so exactly one word in 2^128 is rejected — the smallest possible rejection region.
